title: 12th BRICS Forum in Delhi: Will the Cost Be Public? #Shorts
description:
Should the BRICS forum cost be public? Source: ETV Bharat, ANI.
India hosts the 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum on 26-27 October 2026 in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, New Delhi, as announced by Speaker Om Birla on 22 October. The Speaker called it "a new chapter" in India's parliamentary diplomacy, but we found no cost figure in the coverage so far, and we ask how MPs were chosen and whether India's positions will be reported back to Parliament. A forum on "People-Centric Development" is a good chance to show how open Parliament can be at home too.
Opinion: This is Sawaal's view, not a statement of fact.
Sources: ETV Bharat (22 Oct 2026); OrissaPOST; Indigenous Herald (22 Oct 2026); SocialNews.XYZ (22 Oct 2026); ANI (26 Oct 2026).

script:
ANCHORS: Aditya and Nisha (channel config looks and voices). Real people only as Wikimedia Commons photos (Om Birla). No AI faces or voices of real people. English video; Hindi version made automatically.

FINAL SCRIPT (fact-checked):
[0:00-0:03] ADITYA: "India's Parliament is hosting the world's lawmakers. But who gets to ask the questions?"
[0:03-0:11] NISHA: "The 12th BRICS Parliamentary Forum began on Monday, 26 October, and runs until today, the 27th, in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, New Delhi."
[0:11-0:18] ADITYA: "Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla announced it on 22 October. The theme is 'Strengthening Parliaments for People-Centric Development'."
[0:18-0:24] NISHA: "The government's side: the Speaker called it 'a new chapter' in India's parliamentary diplomacy."
[0:24-0:30] ADITYA: "Fair enough. But in the coverage so far we've found no cost figure. Will it be made public?"
[0:30-0:36] NISHA: "How were Indian MPs chosen to take part, and did opposition MPs get a real role?"
[0:36-0:43] ADITYA: "Should India's positions at the forum be reported back to Parliament? Our view: a forum about people-centric Parliaments should invite questions from Parliament at home too."
[0:43-0:47] NISHA: "Should the cost be published? Yes or no?"
[0:47-0:50] ADITYA: "Every story has a question behind it. Follow Sawaal."

EDIT PLAN (Mr. Cut, 20 shots): 9:16, about 50 seconds, cut every 2-3 seconds. Desk shots, Commons photos (confirm licence and author before export), stock with a "Representative image" tag, and text cards as editable layers for the Hindi swap. Opinion tag on shots 15-17.
